section_summary: This section documents State Department, War Department, and foreign-embassy handling of applications and military clearances for entry into occupied Japan, particularly for traders, officials, dependents, and travelers in transit. Major cases concern Noureddine Naamani, Faez Abdallah Ejel, Roberto Gómez Cisneros, Juda M. Obadia, Emilio P. Virata, the Azrak brothers, and Nicanor Rodriguez y Delgado. The papers also address shore-leave requests, Korean permits, baggage-export rules, SCAP Circular 8 documentation, and changes or extensions to authorized travel dates.

subfiles.title: Action slip for Noureddine Naamani's travel to Japan—file copy
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Department of the Army
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Military clearance and accommodations for Noureddine Naamani's visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Approves sixty days in Japanese-operated commercial hotels and requires two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Action slip for Noureddine Naamani's travel to Japan—signed copy
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Signed military travel clearance for Noureddine Naamani.
subfiles.summary: Confirms sixty-day commercial-hotel accommodations and the requirement for two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Memorandum concerning Morikubo and Watanabe clearances
subfiles.about: Communication of Japanese travelers' clearance information to the Interior Department.
subfiles.summary: Records that Miss Hackett would notify Hawaii's governor so Morikubo and Watanabe could receive travel documents.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Naamani's application
subfiles.about: Submission of Noureddine Naamani's application to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Lebanese businessman's application, apparently under the Inter-Allied Trade Board arrangements.

subfiles.title: Note to the Lebanese Minister concerning Naamani's clearance
subfiles.about: Terms of Noureddine Naamani's authorization to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Naamani may enter between February 15 and March 20, remain sixty days, and use Japanese commercial hotels. The Lebanese Legation is to prepare the statement required by SCAP Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Letter returning Naamani's military permit
subfiles.about: Return of the February 10 military permit for Noureddine Naamani.
subfiles.summary: Returns Naamani's permit and notes that the Lebanese Legation will prepare his Circular 8 statement.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on documenting Japanese businessmen in Hawaii
subfiles.about: Procedure for documenting Honolulu businessmen cleared to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Recommends that Protective Services notify Interior, which would cable Hawaii's governor to arrange documentation.

subfiles.title: Chart of channels for transmitting Japan entry decisions
subfiles.about: Administrative channels for transmitting SCAP approval or disapproval of Japan entry applications.
subfiles.summary: Maps clearance channels for foreign-government applicants, United States citizens, Japanese nationals, and German nationals.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning Husni Halabi's incomplete application
subfiles.about: Missing trade information in Husni Halabi's Japan entry application.
subfiles.summary: Mattar agreed to cable Beirut for details on the goods Halabi intended to trade.

subfiles.title: English translation of Mexican Embassy note concerning Gómez Cisneros
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Mexico
subfiles.about: Request for permission for Roberto Gómez Cisneros to survey Mexico-Japan trade.
subfiles.summary: Requests favorable action on Gómez Cisneros's enclosed application to travel to Japan for a trade survey.

subfiles.title: Mexican Embassy note concerning Roberto Gómez Cisneros
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Mexico
subfiles.about: Spanish original requesting Japan entry permission for Roberto Gómez Cisneros.
subfiles.summary: The Mexican Embassy submits Gómez Cisneros's application in duplicate and requests approval.

subfiles.title: Application of Roberto Gómez Cisneros to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Application for a Mexican government trade survey in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests a one-month Tokyo visit from China to study development of Mexico-Japan trade.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Gómez Cisneros's application
subfiles.about: Referral of Gómez Cisneros's trade-study application to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Requests SCAP consideration and notification of its decision on the Mexican official's application.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum revising Faez Ejel's clearance dates
subfiles.about: Military approval of revised entry dates for Faez Abdallah Ejel.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes Ejel to enter December 5–20 for a twenty-one-day stay and requires two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Conversations concerning Ejel's requested date change
subfiles.about: Faez Ejel's inability to use his original Japan entry period.
subfiles.summary: Keough approved entry between December 5 and 20, and the Syrian Legation agreed to revise Ejel's documentation.

subfiles.title: Note to the Syrian Minister concerning Ejel's revised clearance
subfiles.about: Revised military authorization for Faez Abdallah Ejel.
subfiles.summary: Confirms entry between December 5 and 20 for twenty-one days and requests revised Circular 8 documentation. Ejel must carry two standard passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Commerce letter transmitting revised baggage-export guidance
subfiles.about: Distribution of revised rules for exporting personal baggage and effects.
subfiles.summary: Encloses twenty-five copies of a summary reflecting amended restrictions on food exports.

subfiles.title: General license for exportation of personal baggage and effects
subfiles.from: Office of International Trade, Export Supply Branch
subfiles.about: Rules governing personal baggage, effects, food, firearms, and missionaries' supplies.
subfiles.summary: Defines accompanied and unaccompanied baggage and establishes value limits for foods and soaps. It also limits firearms and gives missionaries higher allowances.

subfiles.title: Conversation on delivery of Korean military permits
subfiles.about: Delivery of Korean entry permits to four Canadian nationals in Toronto.
subfiles.summary: The Canadian Embassy agreed to deliver the permits through official Canadian channels.

subfiles.title: Corporate certification supporting Juda Obadia's travel
subfiles.about: Certification that Juda Obadia represents an American corporation.
subfiles.summary: States that Obadia will travel to Japan to purchase Japanese goods for Genic Export-Import Company.

subfiles.title: Juda Obadia's request for travel documents
subfiles.about: Request for visas and a military permit for travel under a French Moroccan passport.
subfiles.summary: Obadia explains his status, reentry-permit application, and intended late-November Pan American flight to Japan.

subfiles.title: McFadden cover letter enclosing cotton-trade correspondence
subfiles.about: Response to State Department questions about proposed travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a copy of a letter to the Department of Commerce answering State's questions.

subfiles.title: Letter postponing E. O. Taunton's Japan visit
subfiles.about: Postponement of travel because private firms could not yet import raw cotton into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Taunton says a visit is pointless until private raw-cotton imports resume and requests further information.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Geo. H. McFadden & Bro.
subfiles.about: Air-mail envelope for the November 8 correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Postmarked Memphis and addressed to the Department of State in Washington.

subfiles.title: Letter returning Taunton's unused military permit
subfiles.about: Return of E. O. Taunton's permit after cancellation of immediate travel.
subfiles.summary: Explains that Taunton will reapply through Commerce if private raw-cotton trading later makes travel worthwhile.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting suspension of Alfred Goldman's clearance
subfiles.about: Temporary suspension rather than closure of Alfred Goldman's trader clearance.
subfiles.summary: Goldman cannot use his current permit but intends to seek another quota period when his plans become definite.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Alfred Goldman's travel plans
subfiles.about: Goldman's request for longer-term business residence or delayed use of his clearance.
subfiles.summary: Goldman asked that his case remain open while he investigated establishing a permanent business presence in Japan.

subfiles.title: Gordon Agar's application for Japanese shore privileges
subfiles.about: Request for permits for a missionary family transiting Japan en route to India.
subfiles.summary: Agar supplies family passport details and asks that shore permits be sent to the shipping line in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Conversation on shore-leave requests from transit passengers
subfiles.about: Policy toward passengers requesting shore visits during brief Japanese port calls.
subfiles.summary: O'Brien explained that SCAP allowed no sightseeing permits; Weymueller agreed to discourage further applications.

subfiles.title: A. E. Toombs's request for a Japanese shore permit
subfiles.about: Request to go ashore during a Japan stop while traveling to Bombay.
subfiles.summary: Toombs asks for the military permit reportedly required for shore privileges during his ship's Japanese call.

subfiles.title: Conversation on transit-passenger shore leave—file copy
subfiles.about: Duplicate record of the policy against sightseeing shore leave in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Records Weymueller's agreement to stop agents advising transit passengers to request Japanese shore permits.

subfiles.title: Conversation reporting refusal of Emilio Virata's application
subfiles.about: Notification to the Philippine Embassy that SCAP had refused Virata's application.
subfiles.summary: Ruiz agreed to inform Emilio Virata that his proposed entry into Japan had been rejected.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum explaining refusal of Virata's travel
subfiles.about: Military assessment of Emilio Virata's proposed Masonic visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: SCAP found no useful purpose because the Philippine Grand Lodge exercised no jurisdiction in Japan, but invited stronger evidence.

subfiles.title: File note concerning Mr. Kasai
subfiles.about: Status or delivery note concerning Mr. Kasai.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Kasai as an alien residing in Manitou Springs, Colorado.

subfiles.title: Letter returning an undelivered military permit
subfiles.about: Return of a military permit that could not be forwarded to its holder.
subfiles.summary: Returns the permit under the rule that undelivered military permits be sent back to the issuing office.

subfiles.title: Note to the Philippine Ambassador concerning Virata's refusal
subfiles.about: Formal explanation of SCAP's unfavorable decision on Emilio Virata.
subfiles.summary: Explains that Philippine Masonry lacked jurisdiction in Japan and local Masonic leaders saw no value in the visit. A new application could be submitted with positive evidence of necessity and usefulness.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for Juda Obadia's permit materials
subfiles.about: Transfer of Obadia's permit, Commerce certificate, and correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Routes permit number 3850 and supporting papers for action, noting Obadia's French Moroccan citizenship.

subfiles.title: Juda Obadia's Commerce application to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Juda M. Obadia and Philip Zrike
subfiles.about: Business application for Juda Obadia to resume textile trading in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Describes prewar textile imports and plans to visit Kobe, Tokyo, and Osaka for contracts and purchases.

subfiles.title: Letter explaining Genic's corporate succession
subfiles.about: Relationship between Genic Export-Import Company and General Import Company.
subfiles.summary: Explains that prewar Japanese imports were made by the parent company and future trade would use Genic's name.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum approving the Azrak brothers
subfiles.about: SCAP approval for Eduardo and Isidoro Azrak to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Approves the Panamanian merchants for a twenty-one-day December visit and requests selection of a fifteen-day entry window.

subfiles.title: Transmittal slip to the American Embassy in Panama
subfiles.about: Information copy of the note concerning members of the Azrak family.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of the note sent to the Panamanian Embassy concerning the Azraks.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum recommending notification of Azrak approvals
subfiles.about: Proposed notification of SCAP approval for Eduardo and Isidoro Azrak.
subfiles.summary: Reviews the two applications and recommends signing the draft note informing Panama of their approval.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on security information in the Azrak cases
subfiles.about: Verification that adverse information about the Azrak brothers reached SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Keough and Lynch confirmed that Japan received all available security information and decided no further Army action was necessary.

subfiles.title: Note to the Panamanian Ambassador concerning the Azrak clearances
subfiles.to: J. J. Vallarino, Ambassador of Panama
subfiles.about: Entry authorization and documentation for Eduardo and Isidoro Azrak.
subfiles.summary: Reports approval for a twenty-one-day December visit and asks which half of December they will enter. It reminds the Embassy to provide each traveler with the English statement required by SCAP Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Conversation requesting additional Form DS-513 copies
subfiles.about: Philippine Embassy request for fifty Japan-entry application forms.
subfiles.summary: O'Brien agreed to supply fifty additional copies of Form DS-513.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting Forms DS-513 to the Philippine Embassy
subfiles.about: Delivery of fifty applications for permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits fifty Form DS-513 copies requested by Miss McNalley.

subfiles.title: L. Katzman's request for his military permit
subfiles.about: Request for a fifth-group military permit before December travel.
subfiles.summary: Katzman plans to sail from San Francisco aboard the General Gordon and reports obtaining a reentry permit.

subfiles.title: Philippine Embassy note resubmitting Virata's application
subfiles.about: Renewed request for Emilio Virata to visit Philippine Masonic lodges in Japan.
subfiles.summary: States that Virata's office as Grand Master requires official visits to constituent lodges near Tokyo and in Okinawa.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Virata's renewed application
subfiles.about: Referral of the Philippine Embassy's renewed application for Emilio Virata.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Virata's application to the Military Permit Section for further consideration.

subfiles.title: Bombay airgram requesting confirmation of Godet's authorization
subfiles.about: Inquiry about Léon Julian Godet's claimed military authorization to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Godet presented telegrams from French officials in Manila and Tokyo indicating that military permission had been granted.

subfiles.title: Airgram replying on Godet's Japan documentation
subfiles.about: Proper French documentation of Léon Julian Godet's authorization.
subfiles.summary: Explains that French authorities, not the Department, should validate the telegrams and issue the English statement required by Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum on Hussein Touty's extended stay
subfiles.about: Twenty-one-day extension granted to Iranian merchant Hussein Touty.
subfiles.summary: Reports Touty's October 27 arrival and revised departure date of December 8, requesting notification of Iran.

subfiles.title: Note to Iran concerning Hussein Touty's extension
subfiles.to: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Iran
subfiles.about: Notification of Hussein Touty's extended stay in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Touty received an additional twenty-one days and would depart Japan on December 8.

subfiles.title: Montreal despatch transmitting Andrée McGinnis's passport
subfiles.about: Transmission of a Canadian dependent's passport and authorization for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards McGinnis's letter, passport, Army authorization, and proof of December travel priority.

subfiles.title: Andrée McGinnis's letter requesting passport validation
subfiles.to: Passport Branch, Military District of Washington
subfiles.about: Validation of a Canadian passport for travel to join Malcolm McGinnis in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses her passport and First Army authorization and asks for confirmation of embarkation procedures.

subfiles.title: State Department transmittal of McGinnis documents to the Army
subfiles.about: Forwarding Andrée McGinnis's passport package to the appropriate Army branch.
subfiles.summary: Transmits McGinnis's letter, Canadian passport, and First Army authorization.

subfiles.title: Letter delivering Juda Obadia's military permit
subfiles.about: Delivery and terms of Obadia's military permit for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes entry November 16–30 for twenty-one days, requires two photographs, and confirms waiver of the exit-permit requirement.

subfiles.title: Syrian Legation acknowledgment of Ejel's revised clearance
subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of Faez Ejel's December entry authorization.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that the Legation will prepare a replacement statement reflecting Ejel's December 5–20 clearance.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Ejel's third requested date change
subfiles.about: Request to postpone Faez Ejel's Japan entry because of health.
subfiles.summary: Keough required definite dates and warned this would be the final change; Ejel requested December 25–January 10.

subfiles.title: Philippine Embassy note supporting Yusup Abubakar
subfiles.about: Application for Yusup Abubakar to visit Japan en route to Manila.
subfiles.summary: Supports a brief professional visit by a Philippine foreign-affairs officer returning from State Department training.

subfiles.title: Philippine Embassy note forwarding Rodriguez's application
subfiles.about: Submission of Nicanor Rodriguez y Delgado's business application for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests favorable consideration of the enclosed Form DS-513.

subfiles.title: Application of Nicanor Rodriguez y Delgado
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Application to establish a flower and greenhouse business in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Proposes a one-to-four-year Tokyo enterprise serving occupation personnel and transmitting flower orders abroad.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Rodriguez's application to SCAP
subfiles.about: Referral of Rodriguez's application under the other-nations trade quota.
subfiles.summary: Requests SCAP consideration under the Inter-Allied Trade Board quota and notification of the decision.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Andrewses' shore-leave request
subfiles.about: Untimely request by British travelers to disembark at Yokohama en route to Singapore.
subfiles.summary: Notes that SCAP would have denied the request and that the Andrewses had already sailed before State could respond.

subfiles.title: Gennosuke Takahashi's revised departure notice
subfiles.about: Change of Takahashi's sailing date and requested notification of Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Reports a November 28 departure on the Marine Swallow and asks prompt notice so deposited funds can be recovered in Japan.

subfiles.title: Ejel telegram confirming requested arrival window
subfiles.about: Confirmation of Ejel's final requested Japan arrival dates.
subfiles.summary: Requests entry between December 25 and January 10 and promises that no further extension will be sought.

subfiles.title: Airgram confirming continuing military-authorization requirements
subfiles.about: Correction of a reported Swiss claim that military authorization was no longer required for Japan.
subfiles.summary: States that authorization remains mandatory under SCAP Circular 8 and the July 1947 private-trade circular.

subfiles.title: Reference slip from Fisher Howe to Charles Reed
subfiles.about: Blank internal routing slip without substantive remarks.
subfiles.summary: Reference form addressed to Charles Reed with no action marked or remarks entered.
